scope: Independent read-only review of the delivered v0.7 Drive transition and the missing offhand crash. No live process access, native execution or product edits.
conclusion: A zero form weapon is accepted by the trainer and causes the native loader and constructor to omit the second weapon. Native attachment queries contain an unconditional dereference of that missing weapon. This is a proven static fault path consistent with the reported Final Form crash; no crash dump or measured fault PC was available.

claims.Finding: For character1/14 and weapon slot1, selects the form record using signed object-entry byte+87 and reads weapon WORD0. A zero weapon returns objectID0.
claims.Limitations: A valid form index and nonzero model-class WORD+78 are prerequisites; the loader is not itself a safe validation API.

claims.Finding: Form record address is SaveCharacters+3588+56*(form-1), with valid index1..10.
claims.Limitations: Only weapon WORD0 needs the selected fix; changing unlock bits or level is not implied.

claims.Finding: Weapon model resolver uses DWORD table[weaponClass] as word offset, then WORD(item+4) as ordinal; returns DWORD table[offset+ordinal].
claims.Limitations: No native bounds checks or missing-item guard; trainer must validate actual table/model data before a call.

claims.Finding: Resource-load loop resolves weapon slots0 and1; when the resolved model is zero, it skips the recursive weapon resource load and weapon MSET load.
claims.Limitations: A fallback written after resource loading is too late. Loader invokes yield/resource machinery and must remain in native fiber.

claims.Finding: Sora constructor first resolves primary weapon, then for form1..6 or10 resolves offhand. Zero result omits3D7C70 and leaves initialized Actor+3432 null.
claims.Limitations: This omission can be valid for forms whose data never request offhand bones; dual-weapon consumers require a real offhand.

claims.Finding: Loads Actor+3424+8*index and forwards it to3B5D40 without a null check.
claims.Limitations: Actor validity does not establish the required weapon is present.

claims.Finding: First weapon-content access is QWORD[weapon+2744]; a null offhand therefore faults before the event search. It also assumes a suitable type15 event is found before dereferencing event+6/+8.
claims.Limitations: A nonzero malformed weapon or MSET remains unsafe; known valid model and animation mappings matter.

claims.Finding: Actor flag+1736 bit4 selects3D7600 with the incoming weapon index.
claims.Limitations: This establishes actual native routing from generic attachment queries to weapon-dependent data.

claims.Finding: Special bone selectors0x4004,0x4006,0x4008 select offhand index1 through3B5450. Their paired odd selectors select the main weapon.
claims.Limitations: Exact Final Form transition asset/event selecting one of these was not dynamically recorded.

claims.Finding: Weapon MSET name is read from table2AE5A40+32*(slot+2*weaponClass); an empty string means no MSET.
claims.Limitations: Readable memory alone is not proof the asset exists on disk; native loading is retained.

claims.Finding: Weapon construction uses the same per-class/per-slot MSET string, loads the resource and copies parent motion bindings.
claims.Limitations: Constructor assumes valid loaded resources; the trainer must not fabricate a weapon pointer.

claims.Finding: A common action setup checks both main/offhand pointers before applying a flag.
claims.Limitations: Not every consumer crashes; this explains why a constructor can finish portions of the transition before another consumer dereferences the absent offhand.

test_gap: Original fake Begin only manufactured context and form-byte updates; CompleteNative cloned an existing actor without executing the weapon loader/constructor/attachment path. Every form record had level1 and zero weapon. Thus matrix685/0 establishes queue behavior but cannot validate native model initialization.
fix_contract: For dual forms1,4,5, validate existing form weapon plus requested model class/mapping/MSET first. If absent or invalid, plan the currently equipped valid main Keyblade. Do not mutate during preflight. Immediately before NativeBegin, after every other gate passes, apply exactly the record's two-byte weapon field. Keep a valid existing weapon unchanged. Preserve inventory counts and unlock bits. Root elected to leave the repaired record valid after detach/revert; it may be saved by ordinary game saving and must be disclosed.
validation_next: Independent regression include DriveWeaponTests.inl will cover actual resolver-shaped fixtures, missing offhand consumer requirements, preservation and zero mutation on rejection; native runtime effects remain untested.
